stocks.discussion_driver: Deere surged ~4% on August 31 after Baird upgraded to Outperform with an $800 price target—the highest on the Street—calling it the 'cleanest setup' in agricultural equipment. The upgrade thesis centers on a North America row-crop cycle recovery and Fendt brand market share gains that could push EPS meaningfully higher by 2027. The stock is now near its 52-week high, with momentum indicators approaching overbought territory.
bull_case: Baird's $800 Outperform target—well above the Street consensus—reflects conviction in a farm income recovery cycle and North America row-crop demand that DE is best-positioned to capture.
Fendt brand international market share gains and ongoing precision-ag technology adoption provide a durable earnings growth runway beyond the current cycle.
bear_case: Trailing P/E of ~37x is approximately 74% above DE's historical average, leaving limited valuation cushion if ag equipment demand disappoints or commodity prices weaken.
Agricultural equipment demand is highly cyclical and tied to farm income, which remains sensitive to trade policy, weather disruptions, and crop price volatility.

stocks.discussion_driver: Apple gained on August 31 following dual analyst upgrades—Rothschild/Redburn raised to Buy with a $400 target and HSBC to Buy with $366—both citing Apple's AI product pipeline as an 'operational turning point.' The upgrades signal growing Wall Street conviction that Apple Intelligence features will drive a meaningful iPhone upgrade cycle and services acceleration. At $319.70, the stock remains ~7% below its 52-week high, with consensus targets offering modest near-term upside.
bull_case: Simultaneous upgrades from Rothschild/Redburn ($400) and HSBC ($366) reflect growing conviction that Apple's AI integration marks an inflection point for the iPhone upgrade supercycle and services monetization.
Apple's deeply entrenched ecosystem—1.5B+ active devices, high switching costs, and expanding services revenue—provides durable recurring income that cushions hardware cycle downturns.
bear_case: At ~36x trailing earnings (33% above historical median), valuation is stretched and the consensus mean price target of ~$325 implies only ~1-5% upside—leaving little margin of safety if AI monetization timelines slip.

Competition in AI-enabled smartphones from Samsung and Google could limit Apple's ability to command premium pricing, while regulatory pressure on the App Store continues to threaten high-margin services revenue.
